presentingComplaint: New fever, worsening breathlessness, and increased volume of purulent tracheal/sputum secretions on hospital day 6 of admission for an unrelated surgical procedure.
history: 68-year-old man admitted 6 days ago for elective open reduction and internal fixation of a femur fracture, now on the orthopedic ward (not intubated, breathing spontaneously with supplemental oxygen). Over the last 24-36 hours he has developed new fever, increasing dyspnea, and a rise in the volume of purulent sputum with a new cough. He received a single dose of cefazolin for surgical prophylaxis on the day of surgery only. He has no antibiotic exposure in the 90 days prior to this admission and no prior ICU stay. He has type 2 diabetes mellitus and is a resident of the community (not a nursing home). No known colonization with MRSA, ESBL, or CRE organisms. He remains hemodynamically stable, has not required vasopressors, and has no altered sensorium.
examination: Toxic-appearing, mild respiratory distress. Crepitations and bronchial breath sounds at the right lower lung base. No signs of consolidation elsewhere. No rash, no calf tenderness, abdomen soft and non-tender. Surgical wound clean, dry, and healing well without erythema or discharge.
imaging: Chest X-ray: new right lower lobe consolidation not present on admission film
finalDiagnosis: Hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP), day 6, with risk factors for multidrug-resistant organisms
citations: IDSA/ATS Hospital-Acquired and Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia Guidelines 2016
stewardship: Empirical broad-spectrum coverage targeting MDR gram-negatives and MRSA pending culture data: an anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam (e.g., piperacillin-tazobactam, cefepime, or a carbapenem) combined with an agent active against MRSA (e.g., vancomycin or linezolid); de-escalate based on culture and sensitivity results and clinical response within 48-72 hours.
contraindications: Avoid aminoglycoside monotherapy for empirical HAP coverage
Adjust renally-cleared agents (e.g., vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam) if renal function changes
edgeCases: If patient were intubated/mechanically ventilated this would be reclassified as VAP rather than HAP
MDR risk here is driven by hospitalization >48h and current inpatient antibiotic-exposure environment, not by prior antibiotics/hospitalization in the preceding 90 days
Should distinguish from aspiration pneumonia if witnessed aspiration or dysphagia present (not described here)
